executive_summary: The overall intelligence picture today reflects a period of active military operations and strategic repositioning across multiple theaters, with state and non-state actors testing capabilities and adjusting doctrine in response to recent operational experience. The CENTCOM declaration clearing the Strait of Hormuz marks a significant de-escalation milestone following the Iran conflict, though the strategic calculus in the Gulf remains fragile and regional actors like Turkey are simultaneously expanding their precision strike portfolios, suggesting allies and rivals alike are drawing lessons from recent near-peer engagements. Russia's doctrinal shift toward sustained attrition strikes against Kyiv rather than mass salvos indicates an adaptation to Ukrainian air defense improvements and likely reflects resource management constraints, a pattern consistent with how prolonged conflicts force tactical evolution when initial operational concepts underperform. The Pacific Marines action against a suspected drug vessel, while tactically minor, signals an expansion of direct-action authorities in a deployment theater that traditionally emphasized presence over kinetics, potentially foreshadowing a broader remit for military counter-narcotics operations in the region. Notably, the absence of ICS/SCADA/OT reporting today is itself worth flagging, as periods of quiet in critical infrastructure threat reporting sometimes precede coordinated campaigns rather than reflecting a genuine reduction in adversary activity.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: U.S. forces mark a significant milestone in the Hormuz conflict while expanding counter-narcotics operations in the Pacific, as Turkey advances its cruise missile arsenal.

items.headline: CENTCOM declares Strait of Hormuz clear of mines after six-month Iran conflict
items.summary: The U.S. Navy has completed mine clearance operations in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, following roughly four months of active clearing work during the ongoing war with Iran. The declaration signals a meaningful operational milestone, reducing immediate risk to commercial shipping through one of the world's most economically vital waterways. Watch for whether Iran attempts to re-mine or otherwise contest freedom of navigation as the conflict continues.

items.headline: Marines sink suspected drug vessel off Ecuador in first direct action of Pacific deployment
items.summary: A Marine boarding team from USS San Antonio intercepted and sank an alleged drug trafficking vessel off the Ecuadorian coast, marking the Littoral Combat Force-24's first kinetic counter-narcotics action since deploying to the eastern Pacific this month. The operation demonstrates an active enforcement posture in a region where trafficking routes remain heavily active. The pace of future interdictions will indicate how aggressively the U.S. intends to use this force package.

items.headline: Turkey's Roketsan successfully tests ground-launched variant of ÇAKIR cruise missile against dual target types
items.summary: Roketsan conducted its first ground-launch tests of the ÇAKIR cruise missile, validating the system against both land and maritime targets and significantly broadening Turkey's coastal defense toolkit. The ÇAKIR was previously an air-launched system, so ground-launch capability adds a low-cost, flexible strike option that reduces dependence on aircraft for coastal denial missions. This development is relevant to NATO partners and regional competitors monitoring Turkey's increasingly indigenous defense-industrial output.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Today's intel picture is thin on distinct OSINT signals, with the most analytically significant open-source reporting focused on observed shifts in Russian strike doctrine against Kyiv.

items.headline: Russia Shifts Kyiv Strike Doctrine Toward Attrition Over Mass Salvos
items.summary: Open-source tracking of Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv indicates a strategic pivot from large, high-amplitude strikes toward higher-frequency, lower-volume attacks designed to exhaust air defense assets and erode civilian morale. This pattern suggests Moscow is adapting to Ukrainian interception rates by prioritizing resource depletion over single-strike destruction. Watch for whether Ukraine's Western partners accelerate air defense resupply in response to the increased operational tempo.

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: Today's ICS/SCADA/OT threat landscape is thin on high-signal reporting, with no articles from the past 24 hours meeting the threshold for significant operational technology or industrial control system coverage.
